items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he got the bandleader, a fellow named Buster Bennett -- got the bandleader to bring me in.

ctx.x: Well, we worked this club -- we had a regular show -- 6 girls in the line; 2 tap dancers, sometimes Butterbeans and Susie (unintelligible) would work the club. It was kind of a popular little club -- they had a lot of popular little clubs in Chicago then.

But that's when I got my first, real bass violin. I was still going to school, high school, junior high, and Buster got a record date for me. I'll never forget this. And I had to get permission from my teacher to make it, although I'm working every night. We worked from, say, about 9 or 10 o' clock at night until the owner said, Mr. Robinson said, "You could go home now." That means if there were 2 people left in the club, we have to play until they got ready to leave, and it might be daylight. I think I was…
